skim: Indonesian rescuers located the wreck of the Virgo Transport 8 in the Java Sea and deployed the navy survey ship KRI Canopus with underwater drones, as the death toll held at 6 with 129 still missing and a survivor described the ferry tilting with no crew warning.

The Federal Reserve opened its two-day meeting with a quarter-point rate hike — its first since 2023 — widely expected Wednesday, after the 10-year Treasury yield briefly topped 5% and oil’s surge past $108 pushed producer prices up 5.4% year-over-year.

Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, joined by Sam Altman and Elon Musk, renewed calls for a coordinated AI slowdown, triggering a Wall Street rotation that sent CrowdStrike surging as much as 15% while Arm Holdings sank nearly 10% and Nasdaq chip names slid broadly.

Saudi Arabia’s unacknowledged 129-raid air campaign forced Houthi fighters to withdraw most forces from the Bab al-Mandeb Strait after “heavy losses,” even as a tanker was struck near Hengam Island and diesel hit a record $6.06 a gallon.

Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland’s first ministers signed a Cardiff pact demanding independence referendums and closer EU alignment, declaring “Westminster’s time is coming to an end,” as PM Andy Burnham’s office dismissed the threat.

stories.headline: Wreck of Virgo Transport 8 Located as Indonesia Deploys Navy Survey Ship
stories.body: Rescuers located the wreck of the ferry Virgo Transport 8 in the Java Sea and the navy deployed its newest large survey vessel, KRI Canopus, with underwater drones after weather had blocked divers, per Baird Maritime (Sep 15). The death toll held at 6 with 129 still missing and 108 of 243 aboard rescued; Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi confirmed the ferry was “below its maximum capacity of 500 people,” and survivor Agus, a truck driver, recalled “when I woke up, there was no announcement. I only heard from my friends that the ship was tilting,” per LiCAS News (Sep 15).

stories.headline: Only 5 of 76 Palawan Ferry Fire Victims Identified as DNA Teams Deploy
stories.body: A disaster victim identification team from Camp Crame arrived in Palawan as forensic odontologists began extracting molar teeth for DNA analysis from the 71 “totally charred” remains among the MV June Aster’s 76 dead, with only 5 identified so far, per the Inquirer (Sep 13). Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos said President Marcos, attending the BRICS summit in India, ordered agencies to “mobilize the specialists, resources and funding needed,” while the Philippine Coast Guard continues searching for captain Roel Sarmiento, still unaccounted for since the Sep 9 blaze.

stories.headline: ‘People Are Still Afraid of Those Three Letters’: HIV Stigma Persists in Brazil
stories.body: At an International AIDS Conference gathering in Rio de Janeiro, former Welsh rugby star Gareth Thomas said “people are still afraid of those three letters,” per NPR (Sep 12). Brazil has roughly 1.1 million people living with HIV — the largest total in Latin America — with more than half reporting discrimination and 27% diagnosed only at advanced AIDS stage; infectious-diseases specialist Beatriz Grinsztejn and activists including Fabiana de Oliveira described healthcare discrimination and violence against LGBTQ+ people as continuing to deter testing and treatment despite 82% of patients now on antiretrovirals.

stories.headline: Coral Reef Presumed Dead for 60 Years Found Thriving Off Benin
stories.body: Scientists led by Gérard Zinzindohoué of Bénin’s Institut de Recherches Halieutiques et Océanologiques used sonar to scan 11.5 kilometers of seafloor, then an underwater drone and National Geographic’s Deep Sea Camera System to confirm a mesophotic coral ecosystem thriving more than 50 meters down, per ScienceDaily (Sep 14). The team found eight coral species and eight fish species, including golden African snappers and Guinean angelfish; Zinzindohoué said, “I still remember seeing those first images. It was a mix of excitement and disbelief, because after all this time thinking about this reef, suddenly there was something real in front of us.”

stories.headline: Leeds Rout 10-Man Newcastle 4-1 to Climb to Third
stories.body: Leeds scored three goals in a 14-minute burst before halftime — a Lewis Miley own goal, Jayden Bogle and Dominic Calvert-Lewin — then added Noah Okafor’s second-half strike to beat Newcastle 4-1 at Elland Road on Monday Night Football, per ESPN and The Sports Encounter (Sep 14). Newcastle’s defense unraveled after Nico González suffered a concussion early on, handing Matthias Jaissle his first Premier League loss since taking charge; Leeds climbed to third with eight points from four matches, while Newcastle dropped to 12th.

stories.headline: Root Surpasses Tendulkar’s Fifties Record as England Sweep Pakistan 3-0
stories.body: Joe Root struck an unbeaten 62 and set the all-time Test record for half-centuries with his 69th, passing Sachin Tendulkar’s 68, as England chased down 130 for an eight-wicket win at Edgbaston to complete a 3-0 series sweep of Pakistan, per Outlook India (Sep 13). Jordan Cox added an unbeaten 59, and Root became the first player ever to pass 1,000 Test runs at four different venues, joining Jacques Kallis and Ricky Ponting after topping 1,000 at Edgbaston.

stories.headline: Norris Demands VSC Rule Change as Antonelli Opens 81-Point Title Lead
stories.body: After a Virtual Safety Car triggered by Lance Stroll’s stricken Aston Martin cost Lando Norris a likely Spanish GP win at Madring, the McLaren driver is pushing for VSC procedures to be reconsidered, arguing the timing shouldn’t decide races, per Grande Prêmio (Sep 14). Kimi Antonelli, who Toto Wolff credited to the “racing god” for Mercedes’ quick VSC response, now leads the championship 292 points to George Russell’s 211 with nine races left, while Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton retired after six laps with a brake failure.

stories.headline: Fed Opens Meeting With First Rate Hike Since 2023 Widely Expected
stories.body: The Federal Reserve began its two-day meeting Tuesday with a quarter-point rate increase — its first since 2023 — widely priced in for Wednesday’s decision, per Kiplinger (Sep 14). The move follows Monday’s session in which the 10-year Treasury yield briefly touched 5.012% intraday before closing at 4.96%, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.6%, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 5.9%; producer prices rose 5.4% year-over-year through August and traders assigned a 93% probability to a hike, while Brent crude settled 1% higher at $105.68 after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline following drone attacks.

stories.headline: Dell Family Office and Sequence Take Baldwin Insurance Private in $7.7B Deal
stories.body: An entity formed by Sequence Holdings and Michael Dell’s DFO Management agreed to acquire a majority stake in The Baldwin Group for $7.7 billion all-cash, comprising about $4.6 billion in equity and $3.1 billion in assumed or refinanced debt, per Insurance Journal (Sep 14). Existing shareholders will receive $32.50 per share, with closing expected in Q1 2027; Michael Dell said “DFO invests with the flexibility and patience of permanent capital, not as a fund working against a fixed exit clock,” while Baldwin CEO Trevor Baldwin said the firm remains “committed to building the most diversified, vertically integrated insurance firm of the future.”

stories.headline: Oracle Slides 5% as $700M Layoff Costs Overshadow Ellison’s Canceled Stock Sale
stories.body: Oracle disclosed a $700 million increase to restructuring costs tied to “severance and related exit costs” from AI-driven workforce reductions, sending shares down 5% to $142.88, per 24/7 Wall St (Sep 14). The filing overshadowed Executive Chair Larry Ellison’s cancellation of a trading plan that would have allowed up to $7.5 billion in stock sales — the company said “no shares were sold under the plan” and Ellison has “no other plans to sell” — while AI-infrastructure peers CoreWeave and Nebius each fell about 5% in a broader repricing tied to Dario Amodei and Sam Altman’s calls for slower AI development.

stories.headline: Amodei’s AI Slowdown Call Sends CrowdStrike Up 15%, Arm Down 10%
stories.body: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s weekend call for a “coordinated slowdown in frontier AI development” — citing risk of “losing control of AI systems, misuse for cyberattacks and bioterrorism” and pointing to the Hugging Face hack — was echoed by Elon Musk (“Dario is right”) and Sam Altman, who called for “consistent rules to manage frontier risk,” per The Motley Fool (Sep 14). Investors rotated from capital-intensive chipmakers into recurring-revenue software: CrowdStrike jumped as much as 15%, Cloudflare, GitLab and Qualys rallied on the same theme, while SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo and Arm Holdings, trading at 110 times forward earnings, dropped nearly 10% amid added FTC scrutiny of its chip-licensing practices.

stories.headline: Apple Ships Redesigned Siri With Personal Context, Built on Google Gemini Models
stories.body: Apple released iOS 27 with a redesigned Siri that reads personal context from messages, email and photos, answers follow-up questions and can act across apps — letting users, for instance, “locate information contained in an old email” and turn it into a Reminders list, per NetNewsLedger (Sep 15). The new Foundation Models were built “in collaboration with Google and its Gemini models,” ship in English only with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish following in October, and include a Camera mode that answers questions about objects in view across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro.

stories.headline: Revolut Breach Exposes Passports and Bitcoin Histories via Fake Government Request
stories.body: Revolut disclosed that attackers impersonating a government agency — using a spoofed but authenticated official email domain — tricked the fintech into handing over customer passports, selfies, IBANs and transaction histories including Bitcoin records, per BleepingComputer (Sep 14). The company said “Revolut systems and customer funds are unaffected” and that it “immediately blocked the address and alerted the relevant government agency as well as enforcement agencies,” describing the number of affected customers as “very limited,” though crypto investigator ZachXBT suggested high-net-worth individuals were targeted; it is Revolut’s second disclosed breach after one exposed 50,150 customers in 2022.

stories.headline: Saudi Air Campaign Drives Houthis Back From Bab al-Mandeb After ‘Heavy Losses’
stories.body: Saudi Arabia conducted an unacknowledged 129-raid air campaign over 48 hours that forced Houthi forces to withdraw most fighters from the Bab al-Mandeb Strait after “heavy losses,” though ground forces have not fully secured the territory, per GlobalSecurity.org’s Iran War Day 199 update (Sep 14). A Panama-flagged tanker, the El Gaia, was struck near Hengam Island with 14 Indian crew aboard — 13 rescued, one missing — while a fifth consecutive day passed without Iranian ballistic launches, the longest pause since attacks resumed Aug 28; the Oman-hosted Salalah summit remains postponed with no new date, and diesel hit a record $6.06 a gallon as the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut, cutting roughly 700,000 barrels a day.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un Vows ‘Invariable Support’ for Putin as Up to 50,000 Troops Weighed
stories.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un told Putin in a letter released by state media that he is “firmly convincing the victory of the Russian Federation in the present sacred war,” pledging “invariable support to dear friend you and the fraternal Russian people,” per Malay Mail (Sep 15). The message comes amid Ukrainian claims that up to 50,000 North Korean troops are preparing for deployment to Russia, though no timeline was confirmed; South Korean intelligence has previously estimated North Korean casualties in Russia at roughly 2,000 killed, with a more recent assessment putting killed-or-wounded at around 6,000.

stories.headline: Gaza Reconstruction Plan Stalls as Officials Cite Hamas Distrust
stories.body: Officials from the US, Turkey, Egypt and Qatar working on Gaza’s reconstruction, alongside Hamas, described the plan as “not progressing” at a Washington conference, citing deep mistrust and conflicting public and private messaging from Hamas, per the Jerusalem Post (Sep 11). The plan envisions disarming Hamas and deploying 10,000 US-vetted Palestinian police officers atop 1.2 million displaced Palestinians and 370,000 damaged or destroyed homes; officials warned that without progress, both Palestinians and Israelis face the risk of a return to war.

fixtures.headline: Man City Host Sunderland Looking to Bounce Back
fixtures.body: Manchester City host Sunderland at the Etihad on Sep 19 as Pep Guardiola’s side looks to build momentum after the derby win over United.

fixtures.headline: India Open White-Ball Season Against West Indies
fixtures.body: India begin their white-ball season with the first of three ODIs against West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram on Sep 27, ahead of a second ODI in Guwahati on Sep 30.

fixtures.headline: Azerbaijan GP Brings Baku’s Street-Circuit Chaos
fixtures.body: F1 heads to Baku on Sep 26 for a street circuit known for late safety cars, with Kimi Antonelli looking to extend his 81-point championship lead over George Russell.

portfolio.headline: CrowdStrike Surges as AI Safety Warnings Boost Cybersecurity Demand
portfolio.body: CrowdStrike rallied sharply after Dario Amodei, Sam Altman and Elon Musk’s calls for a coordinated AI slowdown reframed cybersecurity as a defensive AI play, per The Motley Fool (Sep 14). The stock trades at 148 times next year’s expected earnings, a premium the article says reflects strong recent quarterly results and CrowdStrike’s position in AI-driven endpoint security.

portfolio.headline: Arm Falls on AI Selloff, Valuation Concerns and FTC Scrutiny
portfolio.body: Arm Holdings dropped in the broader chip selloff tied to AI-slowdown warnings, with the stock’s 110-times-forward-earnings multiple leaving it exposed to a sector-wide de-rating, per Invezz (Sep 14). The FTC is scrutinizing Arm’s chip-licensing practices, and investors are also watching majority owner SoftBank’s leveraged AI investment strategy; Piper Sandler’s Sep 9 Overweight initiation, citing server CPU design wins, has “so far failed to provide lasting support for the shares.”

portfolio.headline: Intel Drops on AI-Slowdown Chip Rout
portfolio.body: Intel shares fell in the semiconductor selloff triggered by Amodei and Altman’s calls to “pace the frontier,” which spread through Asian, European and US chip stocks on concerns over data-center capex, per Yahoo Finance (Sep 14). Piper Sandler initiated coverage this month with a Neutral rating and $110 price target; separately, continued softening of Apple’s use of Intel chips across the Mac lineup has weighed on sentiment.

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare Rallies as Capital Rotates Into Recurring-Revenue Software
portfolio.body: Cloudflare rose alongside Paylocity, GitLab, Commvault and Qualys as investors shifted capital away from AI hardware names on slowdown fears, betting a development pause would let incumbent software platforms “package AI as a feature within their own ecosystems” without the capital intensity of the compute race, per Yahoo Finance (Sep 14). The move builds on a Sep 9 rally after Cloudflare launched an automated vulnerability-scanning tool built with OpenAI’s Daybreak Defense Network.

portfolio.headline: C3.ai Jumps as Software Rally Lifts Beaten-Down AI Names
portfolio.body: C3.ai rose alongside UiPath and SoundHound AI as the same rotation out of chip stocks lifted previously beaten-down enterprise AI software names, per 24/7 Wall St (Sep 14). The move tracked the broader theme of the day: investors favoring recurring-revenue AI applications over capital-intensive infrastructure plays amid the industry’s slowdown debate.

portfolio.headline: Oracle Slides as Layoff Costs Overshadow Ellison’s Canceled Sale
portfolio.body: Oracle fell after disclosing a $700 million increase to restructuring costs tied to severance from AI-driven workforce reductions, overshadowing Executive Chair Larry Ellison’s cancellation of a plan that would have allowed up to $7.5 billion in stock sales, per 24/7 Wall St (Sep 14). AI-infrastructure peers CoreWeave and Nebius fell in tandem, which the article called “a group repricing rather than any single-company issue.”

portfolio.headline: Barclays Falls With UK Banks in Global Bond-Market Risk-Off
portfolio.body: Barclays fell alongside UK banking peers as the global bond selloff that pushed the US 10-year yield above 5% rattled financials broadly; no company-specific announcement was found for the session. The move tracks the same gilt and Treasury-yield pressure covered in today’s Business & Markets section.

stories.headline: Rajouri Police Dismantle LeT-Linked Terror Network, Recover IED
stories.body: Rajouri Police arrested three men — Zakir Hussain, Mohd Azam and Mohd Mushtaq — in the Pir Panjal region for allegedly providing logistical support and safe transit to Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives, recovering an IED disclosed by one of the accused, per Asianet Newsable (Sep 15). Police said the device had been “handed over to the accused by members of a terrorist group for safe custody and its possible use in a targeted attack,” and that the arrested men also served as guides facilitating terrorist movement toward the Kashmir Valley.

stories.headline: India Approves Extended Power Exports to Flood-Hit Nepal
stories.body: India approved extending electricity exports to Nepal following devastating floods, supplying up to 600 MW daily for 18 hours a day through December 31 to cover damage to Nepal’s power infrastructure, per live coverage (Sep 15). The arrangement is aimed at keeping Nepal’s grid stable through the winter as domestic generation capacity is repaired.

stories.headline: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland Sign Cardiff Pact Demanding Independence Votes
stories.body: First ministers John Swinney (Scotland), Rhun ap Iorwerth (Wales) and Michelle O’Neill (Northern Ireland) signed a memorandum in Cardiff calling for independence referendums in Scotland and Northern Ireland and future alignment with the EU, per The Philadelphia Inquirer (Sep 14). Iorwerth declared “there could be no clearer sign that Westminster’s time is coming to an end,” while PM Andy Burnham’s spokesperson dismissed the threat, saying he prioritizes lowering living costs over constitutional debates after previously telling Swinney a Scottish referendum was “off limits.”

stories.headline: Man Dies in 17th-Floor Tower Fire in Poplar
stories.body: One man died and two adults and a child were rescued after a fire broke out on the 17th floor of a 22-storey tower on Blackwall Way, Poplar, in the early hours of Sep 14, per East London Times. Around 70 firefighters from ten engines brought the blaze under control within about two hours; more than 50 residents self-evacuated, and Tower Hamlets Mayor Lutfur Rahman said he was “deeply saddened by the tragic loss of a resident,” with the fire’s cause still under investigation.

stories.headline: Ex-PM Sheikh Hamad Urges Direct Iran Talks, Reactivated Peninsula Shield
stories.body: Former Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani welcomed the planned GCC-Iran meeting in Muscat and called for reactivating the Peninsula Shield Forces — now the GCC Unified Military Command — to protect Saudi Arabia’s borders against Houthi threats, per Doha News (Sep 13). He said “Saudi Arabia’s security is important to all GCC countries, regardless of any disagreements between them,” and proposed transforming the Gulf into an “important economic lake” by removing customs duties between Iran and GCC states.

stories.headline: QNB and Mastercard Issue Syria’s First Internationally Accepted Card in 15 Years
stories.body: QNB Group and Mastercard launched Syria’s first locally issued, internationally accepted payment card in more than 15 years, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 14). Central Bank of Syria Governor Mohammed Safwat Raslan called it “an important step in expanding access to digital banking services,” while QNB’s Khalid Ahmed Al Sada said customers and businesses are “gaining access to international payment capabilities for the first time in more than 15 years.”

doha_events.headline: Qatar Classic Squash Reaches Round Two With Asal, Coll Through
doha_events.body: World No. 1 Mostafa Asal and defending champion Paul Coll advanced 3-0 in the first round at Khalifa International Tennis and Squash Complex, with second-round matches on Sep 15, per Stad Al Doha (Sep 13). American Timothy Brownell pulled off the tournament’s biggest upset, knocking out two-time champion Elias 3-2, while India’s Anahat Singh beat world No. 16 Farida Mohamed 3-2 in the women’s draw; the tournament runs through Sep 18.

doha_events.headline: Frame and Focus Brings VII Foundation Photography to Al Hosh Gallery
doha_events.body: Qatar Museums’ Frame and Focus exhibition opened at Al Hosh Gallery, featuring 13 photographers from VII Foundation programs exploring identity, memory and contemporary life, per Gulf Times. The show runs alongside the museums’ broader fall program of exhibitions across Doha’s cultural venues.

doha_events.headline: Doha Jewellery & Watches Exhibition Returns This Month
doha_events.body: The Doha Jewellery & Watches Exhibition 2026 runs Sep 28-Oct 3 at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre, showcasing luxury jewelry and timepiece collections from regional and international brands.

doha_events.headline: Qatar FinTech Expo Set for Late September
doha_events.body: QFEX 2026, the Qatar Fintech Expo, takes place Sep 29-30 in Doha, bringing together regional banks and technology firms for MENA’s financial-technology summit.
